9	
10	# dev-cli
11	
12	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
13	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
14	
15	```
16	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
17	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
18	herdr / tmux / zellij
19	                a per-host live runtime
20	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
21	```
22	
23	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
24	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
25	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
26	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
27	Machine connection intent has separate owners: OpenSSH remains authoritative,
28	while dev owns only canonical `~/.ssh/dev.d` fragments and explicit generated
29	fleet registrations beside user-authored `remotes.toml`.
30	
31	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
32	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
33	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
34	abandoning a task.
35	
36	## Check it is there first
37	
38	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
39	
40	```bash
41	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
42	dev doctor          # version/install owner/path, PATH collisions, and capabilities
43	```
44	
45	Only **git** is required. System `ssh` enables SSH evaluation/probing/bootstrap
46	and fleet transport; `ssh-keygen` enables key derivation/generation; Windows
47	OpenSSH targets need PowerShell. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
48	Azure CLI enable other capabilities and degrade cleanly when absent — never make
49	a step hard-depend on one unless the requested operation crosses that boundary.
50	
51	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
52	
53	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
54	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
55	
56	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
57	|---|---|---|---|
58	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
59	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
60	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
61	
62	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
63	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
64	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
65	
66	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
67	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
68	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
69	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
70	
71	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
72	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
73	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
74	
75	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
76	
77	## The task lifecycle
78	
79	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
82	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
83	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
84	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
85	
86	```bash
87	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
88	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
89	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
90	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
91	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
92	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
93	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
94	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
95	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
96	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
97	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
98	```
99	
100	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
101	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
102	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
103	
104	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`. Before integrating or deleting an
105	agent-owned checkout, read `references/agent-retirement.md`.
106	
107	### Repository flow preview
108	
109	`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only repository
110	state-machine UI independent of the six-view dashboard. From any canonical or
111	linked checkout it opens the canonical repository and focuses that exact
112	surface; outside Git it opens a picker. It lists every registered worktree plus
113	task-only records, including COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
114	
115	Rows are `canonical`, `managed`, `unmanaged`, `harness`, `task-only`, or
116	`conflict`. Managed bindings receive legal mode/state lifecycle actions.
117	Eligible unmanaged linked rows receive metadata-only Adopt and clean, non-force,
118	branch-preserving Remove Checkout. Canonical checkout removal, harness cleanup,
119	and destructive conflict resolution fail closed.
120	
121	Enter always builds a plan first. The plan separates persisted HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE
122	intent from live facts, shows conditions/remediation/effects/retained resources/
123	fallback, and applies only after `y` or its displayed typed token. Apply locks and
124	revalidates the task revision plus exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact
125	identity; partial effects remain in a result ledger with recovery.
126	
127	`r` reloads local facts without network access. `R` offers explicit fetch,
128	review query, or both; review evidence is run-local and only portable existence,
129	state, draft, URL, provider, and observation time—not decisions or checks.
130	Runtime `none` leaves occupancy unobserved without invalidating otherwise fresh
131	local Git/task facts. The preview omits dirty commit/discard, WIP, shared-writer,
132	takeover, and unknown-runtime overrides; use the displayed CLI fallback when an
133	expert compatibility flag is actually required.
134	
135	## Pick the task's checkout mode
136	
137	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
138	
139	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
140	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
141	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
142	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
143	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
144	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
145	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
146	
147	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
148	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
149	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
150	
151	## Parallel background work
152	
153	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
154	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
155	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
156	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
157	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
158	
159	For a human one-liner, `dev start --run '<shell command>'` uses the same exact
160	new-worktree/root-pane proof and `--focus` independently switches afterward.
161	It does not choose a launcher profile, permission mode, agent name, or wait
162	policy; use the full JSON workflow when those require separate validation.
163	
164	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
165	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
166	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
167	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
168	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
169	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
170	
171	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
172	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
173	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
174	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.
175	
176	## Everyday commands
177	
178	```bash
179	dev                        # interactive dashboard (plain listing when piped)
180	dev note add "thought"     # append to repo containing cwd
181	dev note search "query"    # rebuilds FTS index if needed

191	dev artifact list          # finalization handoffs and receipts
192	dev done --ff              # integrate only; runtime/worktree stay alive
193	dev retire <task>          # external-only close/wait/remove/reap
194	
195	dev git uncommit           # soft reset with a per-worktree message receipt
196	dev git recommit           # reuse that exact message with normal hooks
197	dev git pull-rebase        # exact stash OID + index-preserving restore
198	dev git amend-all          # add -A + no-edit amend; hooks remain enabled
199	
200	dev start                  # context-aware wizard; confirms before creating

205	dev wt list                            # every worktree of this repo

251	
252	Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
253	
254	## SSH host onboarding and fleet registration
255	
256	Read `references/ssh-hosts.md` before changing SSH configuration, installing a
257	key, or registering/removing a fleet host. The safe sequence is explicit:
258	
259	```bash
260	dev ssh init                     # report only
261	dev ssh init --apply             # confirm the one-time Include
262	dev ssh list                     # static; no ssh/Match exec/network
263	dev ssh show lab                 # deliberately runs plain ssh -G
264	dev ssh setup lab --hostname 192.0.2.20 --config-only
265	dev ssh setup lab --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --target-os posix --fleet
266	dev ssh probe lab
267	dev ssh remove lab --fleet       # narrow owned-fragment removal
268	```
269	
270	OpenSSH is authority. Dev reads foreign definitions but never edits them; only
271	canonical portable aliases under `~/.ssh/dev.d` are mutable. Full setup needs an
272	explicit `--key` or `--generate-key`. It sends only one public record to a fixed
273	remote installer, preserves host-key policy, disables connection sharing for
274	proofs, and never copies/reads private key bytes for transfer. A working
275	ProxyJump is skipped unless `--install-on-working-jump` is explicit. Windows
276	administrator authorized_keys needs the separate
277	`--windows-admin-authorized-keys` consent and may still need manual elevation.
278	
279	`--fleet` is never inferred. It writes a strict generated `remotes.d` fragment
280	only after a second fresh ordinary alias login succeeds. The primary
281	`remotes.toml` remains user-authored and is edited through
282	`dev fleet config edit`; `fleet config show` displays the merged config and identifies generated
283	origins. `remote_os` selects POSIX shell or encoded Windows PowerShell transport.
284	
285	Treat partial and unknown results literally. If a remote installer started, the
286	key may have arrived; do not "clean up" `authorized_keys`. Local config and
287	generated keys are retained so a rerun can converge. `ssh remove` never revokes a
288	remote key, deletes local keys/known_hosts, or removes the shared Include.
289	
290	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
291	
292	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
293	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
294	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
295	
296	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
297	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
298	
299	```bash
300	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
301	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
302	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
303	```
304	
305	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
306	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
307	
308	## Creating and setting up repositories
309	
310	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
311	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
312	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
313	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
314	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
315	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
316	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
317	directly.
318	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
319	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
320	exact source tree.
321	
322	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
323	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
324	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
325	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
326	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
327	`start`.
328	
329	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
330	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
331	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
332	
333	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
334	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
335	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
336	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
337	
338	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
339	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
340	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
341	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
342	
343	## Dashboard and forge inventory
344	
345	Bare `dev` / `dev tui` is the seven-view dashboard described here. It is separate
346	from the plan-first `dev flow [repo]` repository lifecycle preview above.
347

481	## Editing configuration
482	
483	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
484	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
485	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
486	
487	## Rules for agents
488	
489	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
490	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
491	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
492	
493	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
494	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
495	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
496	   history unattended.
497	
498	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
499	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
500	   user before overriding it.
501	
502	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
503	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
504	   for them. For merged worktree cleanup, run `dev sweep --merged-worktrees`
505	   from the canonical main checkout, present every candidate and blocker as a
506	   QA question, and use `--apply --yes` only after the user explicitly approves
507	   that exact set. Branch deletion remains a separate `--delete-branches` opt-in.
508	
509	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
510	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
511	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
512	
513	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
514	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
515	   pushed.
516	
517	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
518	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
519	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
520	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
521	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
522	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
523	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
524	
525	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
526	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
527	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
528	
529	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
530	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json` or the same
531	   internal proof used by explicit `dev start --run`. Never infer from
532	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
533	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
534	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
535	
536	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
537	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
538	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
539	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
540	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
541	
542	11. **Cleanup is external, never self-triggered by agent state.** Herdr `done`
543	    means a turn settled. Arm and finalize exact artifacts first; `dev done`
544	    integrates only, and `dev retire` must run outside the target workspace.
545	    Never run raw `git worktree remove --force` against the caller's checkout.
546	
547	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
548	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
549	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
550	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
551	
552	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
553	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
554	   their judgement, not yours.
555	
556	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
557	   configured `paths.state_dir/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes`
558	   and reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation, and `dev`
559	   does not synchronize note/catalog state between hosts.
560	
561	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
562	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
563	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-FTS caches.
564	
565	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
566	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
567	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
568	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
569	
570	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
571	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
572	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.

599	
600	## When to use this skill
601	
602	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
603	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
604	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
605	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
606	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
607	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
608	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
609	- Discovering, inspecting, configuring, probing, or removing an OpenSSH alias.
610	- Installing a public key through ProxyJump or registering a verified dev fleet host.
611	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
612	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
613	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
614	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
615	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
616	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
617	
618	## When NOT to use it
619	
620	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
621	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
622	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
623	  `dev start --json` and explicit `--run` cross-tool launch paths remain here.
624	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
625	
626	## Reference files
627	
628	- `references/ssh-hosts.md` — read before SSH discovery, managed-fragment
629	  changes, public-key bootstrap, probing, or generated fleet registration/removal.
630	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
631	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
632	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
633	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
634	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
635	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
636	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
637	  work moves between machines.
638	- `references/agent-retirement.md` — prepare/finalize/integrate/retire, caller
639	  safety, exact transcript handling and orphaned-runtime recovery.
640	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
641	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
642	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
643	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
644	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
645	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
646	- `references/repository-bootstrap.md` — new/clone/setup presets, project
647	  overrides, skill initialization, upstream publishing, trust and handoff.
648	
649	## Gotchas
650	
651	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
652	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
653	  (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
654	  file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
655	  `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
656	  wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
657	  shell — that is not a bug.
658	- **Windows runs SSH natively but without a multiplexer.** SSH discovery,
659	  protected managed fragments, ssh-keygen, public-key bootstrap, and Windows
660	  fleet transport are supported. There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on Windows,
661	  so the runtime backend is always `none`; `dev fleet open` starts a child shell
662	  instead of replacing the process. Windows remote helpers use only the encoded
663	  allowlisted PowerShell launcher; `remote_os` must match the target. `dev upgrade` self-replaces only
664	  a standalone install and otherwise delegates to the detected Homebrew/Scoop/
665	  `go install` command. Stable releases advance the Homebrew tap; never overwrite its Cellar
666	  binary manually.
667	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
668	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
669	  skips that and leaves you to it.
670	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
671	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
672	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
673	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
674	- **Worktree provisioning and fleet export use different allowlists.**
675	  `[worktree].include` is local-only. `fleet files` reads `[local_files].include`
676	  plus explicit `--file`, expands patterns before transport, and defaults to a
677	  content-free plan. It is not task transfer, backup, restore, or eviction.
678	- **A repository template is a snapshot, not a clone.** Source Git metadata,
679	  remotes and history are excluded. A local Git worktree without a ref includes
680	  tracked plus nonignored untracked files; a non-Git directory includes its
681	  complete current tree. Human plans preview paths and warn about live unpinned
682	  sources. URL userinfo is redacted, while held root/directory/file handles
683	  confine traversal. Symlinks, special files, traversal and source changes fail
684	  closed, and the snapshot applies only to an otherwise-empty new repo.
685	- **Lazygit commit drafts are a best-effort adapter.** `--check-in=stage` writes
686	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in that worktree's Git directory so lowercase `c`
687	  can preload the proposed message. This is not `commit.template` or
688	  `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, uppercase `C` and other clients need not read it, and an
689	  existing different draft is preserved. Draft write/sync failure is a warning,
690	  not rollback: the successfully staged index remains ready for manual commit.
691	- **Agent history remains reviewable.** Built-in `agent-history-hygiene` seeds
692	  `.specstory/.gitignore` only for machine-local `.project.json` and generated
693	  `statistics.json`; it does not ignore `.specstory/history/*.md`. An existing
694	  nested ignore keeps its custom content and mode while missing required rules
695	  are appended. Correct any broader parent `.specstory/` rule explicitly.
696	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
697	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
698	- **Bare `dev done` is interactive only on a TTY.** It reports branch relation
699	  and dirty-content equivalence, then offers commit/discard and FF/PR/merged
700	  handling. It records DONE without closing/removing resources; Retire is
701	  separate. Non-interactive use remains report-only without `--ff`/`--pr`. Unique discard
702	  requires `DROP` or explicit `--dirty=discard --yes`.
703	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
704	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.

13	
14	`dev fleet` fans out over SSH to other machines running their own `dev`, so you can inspect/open their repositories and safely propagate a branch without centralizing their paths, task registries, or runtime state.
15

A missing remote `dev` or unreachable host degrades one row rather than blocking other hosts.

100	## Merge and collision rules
101	
102	- Host names are globally unique across primary and generated layers.
103	- Existing primary profiles may continue to share one SSH alias; this preserves previously accepted configurations.
104	- An SSH alias collision becomes an error when any generated fragment participates. A generated registration cannot silently compete with a primary profile or another managed entry.
105	- Alias comparisons involving generated entries are case-insensitive.
106	- A malformed, insecure, manually edited, or noncanonical generated fragment blocks the merged load.
107	- Defaults are applied after all hosts are merged; generated fragments therefore inherit controller defaults without duplicating them.
108	
109	Use `dev fleet config edit` to resolve a primary collision. Use `dev ssh setup <alias> … --fleet` to reconcile a valid generated fragment; do not hand-edit it.

161	A repository may propose export candidates separately from worktree provisioning:

171	`[worktree].include` is local provisioning policy and is never inherited here.
172	`[local_files].include` also grants no standing permission: an explicit invocation
173	must select exactly one target, and repeatable `--file` adds ad-hoc patterns for
174	that invocation only. Patterns expand on the source into sorted exact paths;
175	no glob crosses the wire.
176	
177	```bash
178	dev fleet files api --to lab                    # report only
179	dev fleet files api --to lab --apply --yes      # create absent target files
180	dev fleet files api --to lab --replace --apply  # authorize differing bytes separately
181	```
182	
183	The source and target must already resolve to one clone with the same normalized
184	**fetch** identity, attached branch, and exact commit. A push-only URL match is
185	insufficient. Both hosts independently prove every exact path is untracked and
186	ignored under their own Git configuration. Only regular files pass: no
187	symlinks/reparse points, directories, sockets, devices, FIFOs, `.git`, nested
188	repositories, or submodule boundaries. Compiled ceilings are 128 files,
189	8 MiB per file, 32 MiB total, with bounded path length/depth; host policy may
190	lower but never raise them. The source branch, HEAD, and fetch identity are
191	revalidated both before and after payload reads; target apply shares the
192	canonical Git-common-directory lease used by `fleet sync`.
193	
194	Plan is the default and sends no file body. Apply additionally requires the
195	configured `machine_id` to match the content-free capability probe. Missing files
196	are atomically created owner-only; identical files are no-ops; differing bytes
197	block unless `--replace` was present in the displayed plan. Replacement binds the
198	observed target digest/mode, retains a private rollback copy, revalidates both
199	roots, and rolls back file changes on failure. `--yes` only answers confirmation
200	and never implies replacement. Public human/JSON output contains path, size,
201	mode, and state—never content or hashes.
202	
203	The transaction journal is durable before manifest/payload staging, so an
204	interrupted request ID can resume or reconcile. Rollback intentionally leaves an
205	empty parent directory when its post-crash identity cannot be proven; deleting
206	another process's replacement would be worse. Native Windows payload transfer is
207	capability-blocked before content is sent.
208	
209	This command is not repository/task ownership transfer, clone acquisition,
210	provisioning, backup, restore, or eviction. It never switches a branch, copies
211	task/catalog/note state, watches for changes, propagates deletions, or removes the
212	source.

The local-host snapshot reuses the current accepted REPOS generation instead of running repository/task/runtime discovery again; if that generation is still loading, FLEET keeps cached rows visible and says it is waiting. `r` supersedes an older request and forces a live reload of every configured host. 271	## Safe branch propagation and degradation
272	
273	```bash
274	dev fleet sync api --push
275	dev fleet sync api                 # HEAD must already equal fetched upstream
276	dev fleet sync api --host lab
277	```
278	
279	The source must be clean and attached. Targets match normalized Git remote identity, not directory name. Each target fetches first; only a clean checkout on the same strictly-behind branch advances by fast-forward. Different branches are not switched. Dirty, ahead, divergent, ambiguous, or unreachable targets stay untouched and make sync non-zero. Hosts without `dev` or that repository are explicitly reported and ignored.
280	
281	Per-host states are `ok`, `stale`, `no-dev`, `unreachable`, `timeout`, `incompatible`, and `invalid-response`. No automatic rebase, force push, background hook, or all-repository pull exists.

109	## Merge 與 collision rules
110	
111	- Host name 在 primary 與 generated layers 全域唯一。
112	- Existing primary profiles 可繼續共用同一 SSH alias，保留先前接受的 configuration。
113	- 任何 generated fragment 參與時，SSH alias collision 就是 error。Generated registration 不能靜默與 primary profile 或另一個 managed entry 競爭。
114	- Generated entry 參與的 alias comparison 不分大小寫。
115	- Malformed、insecure、手動 edited 或 noncanonical generated fragment 會 block merged load。
116	- 所有 host merge 完成後才 apply defaults；因此 generated fragment 可 inherit controller defaults，不需 duplicate。
117	
118	Primary collision 請用 `dev fleet config edit` 解決。Valid generated fragment 請用 `dev ssh setup <alias> … --fleet` reconcile；不要手動 edit。
119	
120	## 透過 `dev ssh` 明確 registration
121	
122	```bash
123	dev ssh setup lab --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --target-os posix --fleet
124	dev ssh setup winlab --key ~/.ssh/id_winlab --target-os windows \
125	  --fleet --fleet-name windows-builder
126	```
127	
128	Alias discovery 或成功 SSH bootstrap 都不會 imply `--fleet`。Setup 最後才寫 fleet fragment，且必須先通過 exact-key verification 與第二次 fresh ordinary alias login。Registered platform 是已驗證的 `--target-os`；managed Windows entry 使用 `dev_path = "auto"`。Remote 缺少 `dev` 仍是 valid SSH onboarding result，安裝前 fleet 顯示 `no-dev`。
129	
130	Partial/unknown bootstrap、failed ordinary gate 或 fleet-fragment collision 都會保留 valid local SSH config/generated keys，但 skip registration；remediation 後重新執行 setup。

244

246	|---|---|
247	| primary `remotes.toml` | durable user-authored fleet intent |
248	| sibling `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` | durable dev-owned fleet intent，只由 explicit SSH commands create/remove |

268	## 安全 branch propagation 與 degradation
269	
270	```bash
271	dev fleet sync api --push
272	dev fleet sync api                 # HEAD 必須已等於 fetched upstream
273	dev fleet sync api --host lab
274	```
275	
276	Source 必須 clean 且 attached。Target 依 normalized Git remote identity match，不依 directory name。每個 target 先 fetch；只有同一 branch、clean 且 strictly behind 的 checkout 會 fast-forward。不同 branch 不會 switch。Dirty、ahead、divergent、ambiguous 或 unreachable target 保持不動，並讓 sync non-zero。缺少 `dev` 或該 repository 的 host 會明確回報並 ignore。
277	
278	Per-host states 是 `ok`、`stale`、`no-dev`、`unreachable`、`timeout`、`incompatible`、`invalid-response`。沒有 automatic rebase、force push、background hook 或 all-repository pull。

40	## High-value structured interfaces
41	
42	```bash
43	dev ls --json
44	dev repo list --json
45	dev repo context [repo] --json
46	dev repo remote --json
47	dev fleet machine-id <host> --json
48	dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host> --json
49	dev repo new NAME --json
50	dev repo clone <ref> --json
51	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
52	dev note list [repo] --json
53	dev note search <query> --json
54	dev note show <note-id> --json
55	<<<<<<< HEAD
56	dev ssh init --json
57	dev ssh list --json
58	dev ssh list --format tsv
59	dev ssh show <alias> --json
60	dev ssh setup <alias> --dry-run --json
61	dev ssh probe <alias> --json
62	dev ssh remove <alias> --dry-run --json
63	=======
64	dev skill list --all --json
65	dev mcp list --all --json
66	>>>>>>> 7b0ec57925f80dc61c6d197ebf5213f7ea39919b
67	dev bootstrap --json
68	```
69	
70	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract. `repo context --json` is an additive schema-v1 report: unavailable facts remain null/error entries with explicit provenance instead of becoming zero values. `fleet files --json` is content-free and never includes file hashes or bodies.
71	
72	`dev skill list --json` keeps its existing array and keys while adding repository, checkout, installation, presence/integrity, registry, and lock metadata. `dev mcp list --json` begins with a `servers`/`diagnostics`/`coverage` envelope; exact Claude local rows add `local_project_path`. Every server field is already sanitized. Declaration state may include Claude's documented project approvals, but must not be interpreted as health or a generally effective merged configuration.
73	
74	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
75	
76	## SSH host and fleet contracts
77	
78	`dev ssh` keeps OpenSSH authoritative while owning only the exact root
79	`Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf`, canonical `~/.ssh/dev.d/<alias>.conf` files, and
80	explicit generated fleet registrations. `ssh init` is report-only unless
81	`--apply` is present. `ssh list` and completion are static and never run `ssh`,
82	`Match exec`, a resolver, an agent, or the network; `ssh show` deliberately uses
83	plain `ssh -G`, and `ssh probe` performs one fresh BatchMode login with connection
84	sharing disabled.
85	
86	`ssh setup` handles new/managed/foreign aliases in one command. Connection flags
87	(`--hostname`, `--user`, `--port`, `--proxy-jump`, `--identity-file`,
88	`--identities-only`) apply only to new or managed aliases. `--config-only` stops
89	after local verification. Full setup requires an explicit `--key` or
90	`--generate-key`; noninteractive full setup also requires `--target-os`, and
91	noninteractive generation requires `--no-passphrase`. Route/platform controls
92	are `--hop-os`, `--install-on-working-jump`, and
93	`--windows-admin-authorized-keys`. `--dry-run` does no OpenSSH evaluation,
94	network access, generation, or writes. `--fleet` is an explicit final step after
95	a fresh ordinary alias login; `--fleet-name` never implies it.
96	
97	Every SSH JSON form emits one object with `schema_version`, `kind`, and stable
98	status/action/error codes; operational failures still emit one safe document and
99	child diagnostics stay on stderr. Kinds are `ssh_init_plan|ssh_init_result`,
100	`ssh_list`, `ssh_show`, `ssh_setup_plan|ssh_setup_result`, `ssh_probe`, and
101	`ssh_remove_plan|ssh_remove_result`. `ssh list --format tsv` emits one definition
102	per row with six fields: alias, status, ownership, source, line, and
103	comma-separated fleet names. See [SSH host onboarding](../guides/ssh-hosts.md)
104	for schemas, partial/unknown outcomes, and the no-private-key/no-revocation
105	boundary.
106	
107	Fleet's durable input is a merge, not one file: user-authored primary
108	`remotes.toml` first, then strict dev-owned sibling
109	`remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` fragments in lexical order, then defaults.
110	`remote_os = "posix"|"windows"` selects the target launcher/path semantics and
111	participates in cache identity. `dev fleet config show` prints the effective
112	merge with secrets redacted and generated origins identified; `config edit` and
113	the TUI edit action continue to open only the primary file. Generated fragments
114	are owned by `dev ssh setup/remove --fleet`.
115	
116	## Repository bootstrap
117	
118	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
119	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
120	reference:
121	
122	| Command | Behavior |
123	|---|---|
124	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
125	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
126	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
127	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
128	
129	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
130	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
131	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
132	
133	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
134	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
135	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
136	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
137	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
138	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
139	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
140	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
141	availability.
142	
143	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
144	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
145	
146	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
147	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
148	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
149	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
150	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
151	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
152	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
153	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
154	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
155	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
156	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
157	  ensures `.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's `.project.json`
158	  and `statistics.json`, never the trackable `.specstory/history/` directory.
159	  Existing custom ignore content and its mode are preserved; only missing
160	  managed rules are appended.
161	
162	After preset selection, the new-repository wizard asks “Customize preset and
163	template options?” with a default of no. The ordinary `agent-ready` flow uses
164	its reviewed template, file, input, and skill defaults without presenting each
165	question. Answer yes—or provide customization flags—to expand those controls.
166	
167	Presets can add typed `string`, `bool`, and `choice` inputs, text templates,
168	hooks, and project skills. Hooks run in fixed `before_commit`, `after_commit`,
169	and `after_remote` phases. The safe hook form is an argv `command`; a shell
170	`run` is explicit, and only `interactive = true` loads an interactive shell.
171	Required failures stop later commit/remote steps; optional failures are
172	reported as warnings. Produced local files are retained for recovery. Native
173	initializers and preset files are repeat-safe; custom hooks and skill setup are
174	responsible for their own idempotency.
175	
176	### Snapshot templates
177	
178	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` seeds a fresh repository from a content
179	snapshot. `SOURCE` may be a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name.
180	For a Git source, `--template-ref` selects an arbitrary branch, tag, or commit;
181	`--template-subdir` selects a clean relative directory as the new repository
182	root. Without a ref, a local Git working tree includes existing tracked files
183	plus untracked files that are not ignored by Git; ignored build/cache content
184	is omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots its complete current tree.
185	
186	The new repository does not inherit source history or remotes. Dev excludes
187	every source `.git` entry, rejects traversal, symlinks and special files,
188	preserves regular-file modes, and validates the complete snapshot before
189	creating the destination. Snapshot files take precedence when the selected
190	scaffold would write the same path; the scaffold still fills missing files and
191	runs the selected initializers. Source and destination traversal is performed
192	relative to held `os.Root` handles, and file bytes come from the already-open
193	validated source handle rather than a second mutable pathname lookup.
194	
195	Confirmation and human dry-run output show a bounded preview of selected paths
196	and warn when a local source is a live working-tree/directory snapshot rather
197	than a commit. Credential-bearing URL userinfo is removed from summaries,
198	structured output, and clone/template errors.
199	
200	Presets expose the same operation through scalar `template`, `template_ref`,
201	and `template_subdir` fields. They inherit normally and explicit CLI flags win,
202	which supports one starter catalog repository plus a child preset for each
203	subfolder.
204	
205	### Check-in policy
206	
207	The interactive wizard offers `commit`, `stage`, and `none`; scripts may also
208	pass `auto`. The behavior is:
209	
210	| Value | Behavior |
211	|---|---|
212	| `commit` | `git add -A`, commit with `--message`/the preset message, then run `after_commit` setup |
213	| `stage` | run `before_commit` setup, then `git add -A`; leave the checkout staged and do not run `after_commit` |
214	| `none` | leave generated changes unstaged and uncommitted |
215	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use `initial_check_in` and compatible `initial_commit`; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
216	
217	In `stage` mode, dev best-effort writes `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in the exact
218	worktree Git directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 reads this
219	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)
220	as the initial message for lowercase `c`; uppercase `C` and Git itself do not use this integration. An
221	existing different draft is preserved and reported rather than overwritten.
222	This is an implementation-detail adapter, not `commit.template`.
223	
224	Staging is the durable outcome: if the optional lazygit draft cannot be
225	written, dev emits a warning and retains the staged index instead of rolling it
226	back.
227	
228	Staged setup cannot create an upstream, and `handoff=start` requires committed
229	setup because a new worktree would omit the staged files. `stay`, `cd`, and
230	`open` remain available for review. `repo setup --commit` is retained as a
231	compatibility alias for `--check-in=commit`; `--message` applies to both commit
232	and stage. Structured results retain `committed` and add `staged`,
233	`staged_paths`, `commit_message`, `commit_draft_provider`, and a content-free
234	`template` summary where applicable.
235	
236	### Upstream publishing
237	
238	Before offering publication, dev probes `gh` and `glab` without changing
239	state. A provider is offered only when its CLI is installed and authenticated;
240	otherwise the wizard gives the relevant installation or login guidance.
241	Local-only is the default, and a newly published repository defaults private.
242	
243	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
244	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
245	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
246	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
247	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
248	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
249	an upstream that was already created.
250	
251	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
252	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
253	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
254	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
255	`--push=false`.
256	
257	### Handoff
258	
259	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
260	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
261	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
262	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
263	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
264	bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. Explicit
265	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches one command only
266	when a newly created first-class Herdr worktree returns its exact root pane;
267	`--focus` independently controls navigation afterward.
268	
269	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
270	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
271	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
272	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
273	line-oriented behavior.
274	
275	## `dev flow [repo]` preview
276	
277	`dev flow [repo]` is an independent full-screen command for interactive TTYs;
278	it has no JSON or non-interactive contract. With no `repo`, a canonical or
279	linked checkout opens the repository identified by the same Git common
280	directory and focuses the exact current surface. Outside Git it opens an
281	asynchronous repository picker. An explicit `repo` overrides cwd.
282	
283	Startup and `r` load only local topology and evidence. `R` offers Fetch refs,
284	Refresh PR/MR, or Both; every choice first creates an exact guarded plan and
285	then requires approval. A provider review observation retains only portable,
286	run-local existence, `open`/`draft`/`merged`/`closed` state, URL, provider, and
287	observation time; it does not represent CI checks or approvals. `runtime=none`
288	remains unobserved and does not expose expert overrides such as
289	`--assume-no-runtime`. See [Repository lifecycle flow](../guides/repository-flow.md)
290	for keys, row kinds, partial ledgers, and the raw-tool escape boundary.
291	
292	## `dev done` finish flags
293	
294	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff`
295	(rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it), `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge
296	request), or `--merged` (verify external integration against `--base-ref`).
297	Omitting an integration choice opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY —
298	see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the
299	prompts.
300	
301	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
302	
303	| Value | Behavior |
304	|---|---|
305	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
306	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
307	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
308	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
309	
310	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a
311	non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive
312	confirmation step. `--push` pushes the branch or base selected by the
313	integration mode. Successful local or externally verified integration records
314	DONE/MERGED while always retaining the runtime, worktree, and branch for a
315	separate `dev retire`; `--keep-worktree` remains only as a no-op compatibility
316	warning, while `--delete-branch` fails with guidance to use
317	`dev retire --delete-branch`. `--merged` can use
318	`--confirm-squash <merge-commit>` as explicit operator attestation for a squash
319	result; provider status never implies that attestation.
320	
321	## Configuration
322	
323	```bash
324	dev config init
325	dev config show
326	dev config path
327	dev config scaffolds init
328	dev config scaffolds show
329	dev config scaffolds path
330	dev config scaffolds edit
331	
332	dev fleet config init      # user-authored primary remotes.toml
333	dev fleet config show      # effective primary + generated remotes.d merge
334	dev fleet config edit      # primary only
335	dev ssh init               # report dedicated OpenSSH Include plan
336	dev ssh init --apply       # install it after confirmation
337	```
338	
339	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
340	
341	Key sections:
342	
343	| Section | Controls |
344	|---|---|
345	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
346	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
347	| `[worktree]` | local ignored-file provisioning, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
348	| `[local_files]` | host ceilings for portable files; project overlays provide the separate off-machine candidate allowlist |
349	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
350	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
351	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
352	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
353	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
354	
355	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
356	trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
357	The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
358	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
359	payloads. It is not configuration,
360	cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
361	optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
362	has returned.
363	
364	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
365	
366	### Scaffold presets
367	
368	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
369	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
370	A compact preset looks like:
371	
372	```toml
373	version = 1
374	default_preset = "team"
375	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
376	
377	[presets.team]
378	extends = "agent-ready"
379	handoff = "cd"
380	initial_check_in = "stage"
381	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
382	template_ref = "v2"
383	template_subdir = "services/go"
384	
385	[[presets.team.inputs]]
386	id = "deployment"
387	type = "choice"
388	choices = ["none", "docker"]
389	default = "none"
390	
391	[[presets.team.files]]
392	id = "service-readme"
393	source = "service/README.md" # templates/service/README.md beside this file
394	destination = "docs/service.md"
395	
396	[[presets.team.hooks]]
397	id = "verify"
398	phase = "before_commit"
399	command = ["make", "test"]
400	required = true
401	
402	[[presets.team.skills]]
403	id = "knowledge"
404	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
405	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
406	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
407	default = true
408	
409	[presets.team.skills.setup]
410	phase = "before_commit"
411	interpreter = "bash"
412	script = "scripts/init.sh"
413	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
414	required = true
415	```
416	
417	Skill setup normally names a project-local script inside the installed skill.
418	The shipped recommendations instead use `builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` or
419	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`; these fixed reviewed initializers do
420	not execute downloaded skill code.
421	
422	A preset may extend one parent. Scalars override; simple lists replace; files,
423	hooks, and skills merge by `id`, and an inherited item can be disabled with
424	`enabled = false`. A `[[presets.*.files]]` rendering source must remain in the
425	`templates/` tree next to its config source; that file-level mechanism is
426	separate from the repository snapshot `template` scalar above. Destinations
427	must remain inside the repository, and a skill setup script must remain inside
428	the installed skill directory. `initial_check_in` accepts `commit`, `stage`, or
429	`none`; the legacy `initial_commit` boolean remains readable, but a preset must
430	not set both.
431	
432	### Safe project overlays
433	
434	A repository may commit these fixed files:
435	
436	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning, separately
437	  proposed portable local-file patterns, and repository setup wizard defaults.
438	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`: project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
439	  setup using the same versioned schema.
440	
441	```toml
442	# .dev-cli/config.toml
443	version = 1
444	
445	[worktree]
446	include = [".env.example"]
447	strategy = "reinstall"
448	
449	# Proposed candidates only; export still requires explicit fleet files --to.
450	[local_files]
451	include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
452	
453	[repo.setup]
454	preset = "team"
455	handoff = "cd"
456	check_in = "stage"
457	```
458	
459	Effective precedence, lowest to highest, is built-ins, global config/scaffolds,
460	legacy `.dev.toml`, the target repository's `.dev-cli/*`, then explicit CLI or
461	wizard choices. `.dev.toml` remains readable for compatibility; new project
462	configuration should use `.dev-cli/config.toml`. Global `default_preset` and the
463	project `[repo.setup]` preset, handoff, and check-in fields seed interactive
464	wizard choices; they do not change scripted defaults, which are controlled by
465	the corresponding flags. The legacy `commit` boolean remains readable, but may
466	not be combined with `check_in` in the same layer.
467	
468	`[local_files].include` never inherits `[worktree].include`: provisioning a local checkout is not authorization to export a secret. Project overlays may propose only the portable include list; host-owned count/size/path ceilings come from global config and cannot be raised by a repository. The command remains report-only until an explicit `--apply`, target pin, and confirmation.
469	
470	Project files cannot override host paths, state location, runtime backend,
471	forge inventory or credentials, stats, update, bootstrap, or TUI policy. They
472	also cannot silently publish a repository. Before a post-create command from
473	`.dev-cli/config.toml`, or a hook or skill setup from project
474	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, executes, dev asks to trust the canonical repository
475	plus an execution-content hash. Changed executable content requires new
476	consent; non-interactive use without a matching trust record fails closed.
477	Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Keep credentials and
478	host-specific paths in user config or ignored environment files, never in a
479	committed project overlay.
480	
481	Project-authored skill setup must use a local source so its bytes can be bound
482	to the trust hash. Remote project skills may still be installed, but cannot
483	declare executable setup; global presets remain host-owned policy.
484	
485	## Colored output
486	
487	Every human-readable surface applies semantic ANSI color through a small set of roles: `title`/`header`/`prompt` (bold cyan), `label`/`dim` (dim), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `danger` (bold red), `review` (magenta, for a PR/review handoff), and `strong`/`code` for Markdown. Values that carry their own meaning are colored by that meaning rather than by a fixed role:
488	
489	| Value | Green | Yellow | Red |
490	|---|---|---|---|
491	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, `no checkout` | `conflict`, `error` |
492	| Task state | `hot`, `done` | `warm`, `cold`, `parked` | — |
493	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`, `no-dev` | `unreachable`, `timeout`, `incompatible` |
494	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`, `failed` |
495	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`, `finalizing` | `failed` |
496	
497	`dev journal` and `dev summary` emit Markdown, so their headings and fenced code blocks are styled the same way `dev help <topic>` styles a quick-reference page. In command help, only the names you can type — command names and flag specs — are colored; descriptions stay plain, and the column alignment cobra computes is unaffected because a terminal gives an escape sequence no width.
498	
499	Control it with the global `--color <auto|always|never>` flag (default `auto`). `auto` disables color when output is not attached to a terminal, when `NO_COLOR` is set to any non-empty value, or when `TERM=dumb`. The setting reaches the interactive dashboard as well, so `dev --color never` renders it without color. `--json` output is never colored regardless of mode. There is no config-file field for color — `--color` and the environment are the only controls, so piping `dev` never requires `--color never` to stay clean.
500	
501	## Shell integration
502	
503	```bash
504	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"
505	dev shell-init fish | source
506	```
507	
508	The trusted `shell-init` output defines a wrapper because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. 80	## SSH host 與 fleet contracts
81	
82	`dev ssh` 維持 OpenSSH authority，只擁有 exact root
83	`Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf`、canonical `~/.ssh/dev.d/<alias>.conf` files，以及
84	explicit generated fleet registration。`ssh init` 沒有 `--apply` 時只回報。
85	`ssh list` 與 completion 都是 static，絕不執行 `ssh`、`Match exec`、resolver、
86	agent 或 network；`ssh show` 刻意使用 plain `ssh -G`，`ssh probe` 則執行一次
87	sharing disabled 的 fresh BatchMode login。
88	
89	`ssh setup` 用一個 command 處理 new/managed/foreign alias。Connection flags
90	（`--hostname`、`--user`、`--port`、`--proxy-jump`、`--identity-file`、
91	`--identities-only`）只適用 new 或 managed alias。`--config-only` 在 local
92	verification 後停止。Full setup 必須 explicit `--key` 或 `--generate-key`；
93	noninteractive full setup 還需要 `--target-os`，noninteractive generation 需要
94	`--no-passphrase`。Route/platform controls 是 `--hop-os`、
95	`--install-on-working-jump` 與 `--windows-admin-authorized-keys`。`--dry-run`
96	不執行 OpenSSH evaluation、network access、generation 或 write。`--fleet` 是
97	fresh ordinary alias login 後才執行的 explicit final step；`--fleet-name` 不會
98	imply 它。

100	每個 SSH JSON form 都輸出一個含 `schema_version`、`kind` 與 stable

102	child diagnostic 留在 stderr。Kinds 是 `ssh_init_plan|ssh_init_result`、
103	`ssh_list`、`ssh_show`、`ssh_setup_plan|ssh_setup_result`、`ssh_probe` 與
104	`ssh_remove_plan|ssh_remove_result`。`ssh list --format tsv` 每個 definition 一列，
105	共有六欄：alias、status、ownership、source、line、comma-separated fleet names。
106	Schema、partial/unknown outcome 與 no-private-key/no-revocation boundary 請見

169	### Snapshot templates
170	
171	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` 會用 content snapshot 建立全新 repository。
172	`SOURCE` 可為 local directory/repository、Git URL 或 owner/name。Git source 可用
173	`--template-ref` 指定任意 branch、tag 或 commit；`--template-subdir` 則指定作為新
174	repository root 的乾淨 relative directory。未指定 ref 時，local Git working tree 會
175	包含現存 tracked files，以及未被 Git ignore 的 untracked files；ignored build/cache
176	content 會省略。Non-Git directory 則 snapshot 完整 current tree。
177	
178	新 repository 不會繼承 source history 或 remotes。Dev 會排除每個 source `.git`
179	entry、拒絕 traversal、symlink 與 special files、保留 regular-file modes，並在建立
180	destination 前驗證完整 snapshot。若 snapshot 與 selected scaffold 寫入同一路徑，
181	snapshot 優先；scaffold 仍會補齊缺少的 files 並執行 selected initializers。
182	Source 與 destination traversal 都相對於 held `os.Root` handles 進行；file bytes 來自
183	已開啟且驗證過的 source handle，不會再次依 mutable pathname lookup。
184	
185	Confirmation 與 human dry-run output 會顯示 bounded selected-path preview；local source
186	若是 live working-tree/directory snapshot 而非 commit，也會明確 warning。含 credential
187	的 URL userinfo 會從 summaries、structured output 與 clone/template errors 移除。
188	
189	Preset 可用 scalar `template`、`template_ref`、`template_subdir` 宣告同一操作。它們依
190	一般 inheritance 規則 resolve，explicit CLI flags 優先，因此可以一個 starter catalog
191	repository 搭配每個 subfolder 各一個 child preset。
192	
193	### Check-in policy
194	
195	Interactive wizard 提供 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；script 也可傳 `auto`：
196	
197	| 值 | 行為 |
198	|---|---|
199	| `commit` | `git add -A`，以 `--message`／preset message commit，再執行 `after_commit` setup |
200	| `stage` | 執行 `before_commit` setup 後 `git add -A`；保留 staged checkout，不執行 `after_commit` |
201	| `none` | generated changes 保持 unstaged、uncommitted |
202	| `auto` | `repo new` 使用 `initial_check_in` 與相容的 `initial_commit`；clone/setup 則不自動 check-in |
203	
204	`stage` mode 會 best-effort 在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入
205	`LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`。[Lazygit v0.59.0 會讀取此
206	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，並將它作為小寫 `c` 的 initial message；大寫
207	`C` 與 Git 本身不使用此 integration。不同內容的既有 draft 會保留並回報 warning，
208	不會被覆寫。這是 implementation-detail adapter，不是 `commit.template`。
209	
210	Staging 才是 durable outcome：optional lazygit draft 若無法寫入，dev 會發出 warning
211	並保留 staged index，不會 rollback。
212	
213	Staged setup 不能建立 upstream；`handoff=start` 也要求已 commit 的 setup，因為新
214	worktree 會漏掉 staged files。`stay`、`cd`、`open` 仍可供 review。`repo setup
215	--commit` 保留為 `--check-in=commit` 的 compatibility alias；`--message` 同時適用於
216	commit 與 stage。Structured result 保留 `committed`，並在適用時加入 `staged`、
217	`staged_paths`、`commit_message`、`commit_draft_provider` 與不含 file content 的
218	`template` summary。
219	
220	### Upstream publishing
221	
222	提供 publishing 選項前，dev 會以 read-only 方式 probe `gh` 與 `glab`。只有 CLI 已
223	安裝且完成 authentication 的 provider 才會出現；否則 wizard 顯示對應的安裝或 login
224	指引。預設 local-only，新 publish 的 repository 預設 private。
225	
226	Publishing 會沿用 local repository name 與 configured description，再詢問 provider
227	namespace/owner、visibility，以及是否 push initial/current branch。Dev 會在必要的
228	local setup 與 commit steps 成功後建立空的 GitHub 或 GitLab repository，再新增／驗證
229	`origin`，並可選擇以 upstream tracking push。Provider、name-conflict 或 push failure
230	絕不刪除 local checkout，也不會刪除已建立的 upstream。
231	
232	從 `repo setup` publish 時必須使用 `--check-in=commit`（或相容的 `--commit` flag），
233	避免新建 upstream 漏掉本次產生的 setup changes。`--check-in=stage` 與任何新 upstream
234	不相容；對新 repository 而言，`none` 只有搭配 `--push=false` 才能建立刻意保持空白的
235	upstream。
236	
237	### Handoff
238	
239	`stay` 只輸出結果；`cd` 透過受信任的 `shell-init` wrapper 改變 parent shell；
240	`open` 開啟 configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime，runtime 為 `none` 時退回 `cd`；
241	`start` 會固定此 repository 並接續現有 task wizard。Setup 留下 uncommitted files、
242	導致新 worktree 會遺漏它們時，`start` 不可用。Repository bootstrap 與
243	預設的 `dev start` 都不會啟動 coding agent。明確使用 worktree mode 的
244	`dev start --run '<shell command>'` 時，只有本次新建 first-class Herdr worktree
245	回傳 exact root pane 才會 dispatch command；之後是否轉跳仍由 `--focus` 獨立控制。
246	
247	Repository、task-start 與 finish wizard 共用的 TTY text fields 都使用 inline editor：
248	Left/Right、Home/End、Delete/Backspace、cursor 位置插入與 Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation 會
249	被解讀為 terminal actions，不會成為 raw escape bytes。Buffered 或 piped non-TTY input
250	仍維持 line-oriented behavior。
251	
252	## `dev flow [repo]` preview
253	
254	`dev flow [repo]` 是獨立 full-screen command，只接受 interactive TTY；它沒有 JSON/non-interactive contract。省略 `repo` 時，canonical/linked checkout 會開啟同一 Git common-directory repository 並 focus exact current surface；Git 之外則非同步開 repository picker。明確 `repo` 會覆蓋 cwd。
255	
256	Startup 與 `r` 只載入 local topology/evidence。`R` 才提供 Fetch refs、Refresh PR/MR 或 Both；每個 choice 都先產生 exact guarded plan，再要求 approval。Provider review observation 只在 current run 保存最低限度的 existence、`open`/`draft`/`merged`/`closed`、URL、provider 與 observed time，不代表 CI checks 或 approvals。`runtime=none` 保持 unobserved，也不提供 `--assume-no-runtime` 等 expert override。詳細 keys、row kinds、partial ledger 與 escape boundary 見 [Repository Flow 預覽](../guides/repository-flow.zh-TW.md)。
257	
258	## `dev done` finish flags
259	
260	`dev done` 對 branch/worktree task 透過 `--ff`（rebase 到 base 再 fast-forward）、`--pr`（push 並開啟 pull/merge request）或 `--merged`（依 `--base-ref` 驗證外部 integration）處理。未指定 integration choice 時，在 TTY 上會開啟 interactive finish wizard —— 提示內容見[變更流工作流程](../guides/change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
261	
262	Dirty checkout 由 `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` 處理（預設 `auto`）：
263	
264	| 值 | 行為 |
265	|---|---|
266	| `auto` | interactive：提示 commit 或 discard；non-interactive：直接失敗，等同 `fail` |
267	| `fail` | dirty checkout 時拒絕 finish |
268	| `commit` | 用 `--message`/`-m` commit 全部變更（未指定時 interactive 會提示輸入） |
269	| `discard` | reset tracked 變更並移除 untracked files；具破壞性，沒有 TTY 時需要 `--yes` |
270	
271	`--yes`/`-y` 用來確認選定的 finish plan；non-interactive 的 `--dirty discard` 必須要有它，其他情況則是跳過 interactive 確認步驟。`--push` 會依 selected integration push 對應 branch/base。成功的 local 或 externally verified integration 只記錄 DONE/MERGED，永遠保留 runtime、worktree 與 branch 給獨立的 `dev retire`；`--keep-worktree` 只保留為 no-op compatibility warning，`--delete-branch` 則會報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`。`--merged` 可用 `--confirm-squash <merge-commit>` 對 squash result 作明確 operator attestation，不能由 provider status 自動推斷。
272	
273	## Configuration
274	
275	```bash
276	dev config init
277	dev config show
278	dev config path
279	dev config scaffolds init
280	dev config scaffolds show
281	dev config scaffolds path
282	dev config scaffolds edit
283	
284	dev fleet config init      # user-authored primary remotes.toml
285	dev fleet config show      # effective primary + generated remotes.d merge
286	dev fleet config edit      # primary only
287	dev ssh init               # report dedicated OpenSSH Include plan
288	dev ssh init --apply       # confirmation 後安裝

290	
291	`config init` 偵測 local roots 並寫出 explicit defaults。Config file 不存在仍可運作；built-in defaults 讓核心 Git behavior 可用，但 generated config 能讓 machine policy 可 review，因此較推薦。
292	
293	主要 sections：
294	
295	| Section | 控制內容 |
296	|---|---|
297	| `[paths]` | scan roots、project/tries/worktree roots、worktree template、state path |
298	| `[runtime]` | `auto`、Herdr、tmux、Zellij 或 none，以及 metadata settings |
299	| `[worktree]` | local ignored-file provisioning、linked dirs、setup commands、strategies、timeout |
300	| `[local_files]` | portable files 的 host ceilings；project overlay 提供獨立的 off-machine candidate allowlist |
301	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | 完整 remote inventory 的 cache TTL，以及 opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
302	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion、symlink handling、index/layout policy |
303	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns、sorting 與 external-tool bindings |
304	| `[stats]` | sampler 與 optional WakaTime import |
305	| `[update]` | `check`（預設 `true`）— 允許每天一次的「有新版」提示與其背景 cache refresh；`DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可覆寫 |
306	
307	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` 會啟用單次 TUI startup/readiness trace。
308	Target 必須是 absolute 且尚不存在；dev 絕不 overwrite。Private、bounded document
309	在 TUI teardown 後才寫入，只包含 relative categorical timings 與 aggregate row
310	counts，不包含 names、paths 或 raw payloads；它不是 configuration、cache、durable
311	stats、stdout 或 network telemetry。
312	Dashboard 與 `dev flow` 這類 full-screen invocation 的 optional update-cache network refresh 也會延後到 initial view return 之後；這不會把 Flow 自己的 local `r` 變成 remote refresh。
313	
314	Repository quick-note Markdown 是 configured `paths.state_dir/notes` 下的 durable data；該路徑預設為 `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`。`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` 的 full-text index 是 disposable，會從 Markdown 重建；調整 `paths.state_dir` 不會移動 cache。
315	
316	### Scaffold presets
317	
318	Global repository recipes 位於 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`（或 root
319	`--scaffolds` override）。每個 authored file 都必須宣告 `version = 1`。精簡 preset
320	範例：
321	
322	```toml
323	version = 1
324	default_preset = "team"
325	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
326	
327	[presets.team]
328	extends = "agent-ready"
329	handoff = "cd"
330	initial_check_in = "stage"
331	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
332	template_ref = "v2"
333	template_subdir = "services/go"
334	
335	[[presets.team.inputs]]
336	id = "deployment"
337	type = "choice"
338	choices = ["none", "docker"]
339	default = "none"
340	
341	[[presets.team.files]]
342	id = "service-readme"
343	source = "service/README.md" # 此檔案旁的 templates/service/README.md
344	destination = "docs/service.md"
345	
346	[[presets.team.hooks]]
347	id = "verify"
348	phase = "before_commit"
349	command = ["make", "test"]
350	required = true
351	
352	[[presets.team.skills]]
353	id = "knowledge"
354	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
355	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
356	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
357	default = true
358	
359	[presets.team.skills.setup]
360	phase = "before_commit"
361	interpreter = "bash"
362	script = "scripts/init.sh"
363	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
364	required = true
365	```
366	
367	Skill setup 一般會指定 installed skill 內的 project-local script。內建推薦項目則使用
368	`builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` 或
369	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`；這些固定且經 review 的 initializer 不會執行
370	下載回來的 skill code。
371	
372	Preset 最多 extend 一個 parent。Scalar 會 override；simple lists 會 replace；files、
373	hooks 與 skills 依 `id` merge，inherited item 可用 `enabled = false` 停用。
374	`[[presets.*.files]]` 的 rendering source 必須留在 config source 旁的 `templates/`
375	tree；這個 file-level mechanism 與前述 repository snapshot `template` scalar 不同。
376	Destination 必須留在 repository 內，skill setup script 也必須位於 installed skill
377	directory 內。`initial_check_in` 接受 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；legacy
378	`initial_commit` boolean 仍可讀，但同一 preset 不可同時設定兩者。
379	
380	### Safe project overlays
381	
382	Repository 可 commit 兩個固定檔案：
383	
384	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`：allowlisted worktree provisioning、分開提出的 portable
385	  local-file patterns 與 repository setup wizard defaults。
386	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`：使用同一 versioned schema 的 project presets、
387	  templates、hooks 與 skill setup。
388	
389	```toml
390	# .dev-cli/config.toml
391	version = 1
392	
393	[worktree]
394	include = [".env.example"]
395	strategy = "reinstall"
396	
397	# 只提出 candidates；export 仍需 explicit fleet files --to。
398	[local_files]
399	include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
400	
401	[repo.setup]
402	preset = "team"
403	handoff = "cd"
404	check_in = "stage"
405	```
406	
407	Effective precedence 由低至高為 built-ins、global config/scaffolds、legacy
408	`.dev.toml`、target repository 的 `.dev-cli/*`，最後是 explicit CLI 或 wizard
409	choices。`.dev.toml` 為相容性仍可讀；新的 project configuration 應使用
410	`.dev-cli/config.toml`。Global `default_preset` 與 project `[repo.setup]` 的 preset、
411	handoff、check-in fields 只用來預填 interactive wizard choices；它們不會改變
412	scripted defaults，後者由對應 flags 控制。Legacy `commit` boolean 仍可讀，但同一
413	layer 不可與 `check_in` 並用。
414	
415	`[local_files].include` 絕不繼承 `[worktree].include`：佈建 local checkout 不等於授權 export secret。Project overlay 只能提出 portable include list；host-owned count/size/path ceilings 來自 global config，repository 不能提高。Command 仍保持 report-only，直到 explicit `--apply`、target pin 與 confirmation 都具備。
416	
417	Project files 不能 override host paths、state location、runtime backend、forge
418	inventory 或 credentials、stats、update、bootstrap 或 TUI policy，也不能靜默 publish
419	repository。執行來自 `.dev-cli/config.toml` 的 post-create command，或來自 project
420	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 的 hook／skill setup 前，dev 會依 canonical repository 加
421	execution-content hash 詢問 trust；executable content 變更後必須重新同意，
422	non-interactive 且沒有 matching trust record 時 fail closed。Legacy `.dev.toml` 保留其
423	compatibility behavior。Credential 與 host-specific path 應放 user config 或 ignored
424	environment file，絕不放 committed project overlay。
425	
426	Project-authored skill setup 必須使用 local source，讓實際 bytes 能納入 trust hash。
427	Remote project skill 仍可安裝，但不能宣告 executable setup；global preset 則仍屬於
428	host-owned policy。
429	
430	## 彩色輸出
431	
432	所有 human-readable 介面都透過一組 semantic role 套用 ANSI color：`title`/`header`/`prompt`（bold cyan）、`label`/`dim`（dim）、`success`（green）、`warning`（yellow）、`danger`（bold red）、代表 PR/review handoff 的 `review`（magenta），以及 Markdown 用的 `strong`/`code`。本身帶有意義的值依其意義上色，而非固定 role：
433	
434	| 值 | 綠色 | 黃色 | 紅色 |
435	|---|---|---|---|
436	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`、`ahead`、`behind`、`no checkout` | `conflict`、`error` |
437	| Task state | `hot`、`done` | `warm`、`cold`、`parked` | — |
438	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`、`no-dev` | `unreachable`、`timeout`、`incompatible` |
439	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`、`failed` |
440	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`、`finalizing` | `failed` |
441	
442	`dev journal` 與 `dev summary` 輸出 Markdown，因此其 heading 與 fenced code block 的樣式與 `dev help <topic>` 的 quick-reference 頁面相同。在 command help 中只有你會實際輸入的名稱 —— command 名稱與 flag spec —— 會上色；description 保持原色，且 cobra 計算出的欄位對齊不受影響，因為 terminal 不會給 escape sequence 任何寬度。
443	
444	用全域的 `--color <auto|always|never>` flag 控制（預設 `auto`）。`auto` 在 output 未連接 terminal、`NO_COLOR` 被設為任何非空值，或 `TERM=dumb` 時會停用 color。此設定同樣會傳到 interactive dashboard，因此 `dev --color never` 也會讓儀表板不上色。`--json` output 不論 mode 為何都不會上色。目前沒有對應的 config-file 欄位 —— `--color` 與 environment 是僅有的控制方式，因此 pipe `dev` 的輸出不需要額外傳 `--color never` 就是乾淨的。
445	## Shell integration
446	
447	```bash
448	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"
449	dev shell-init fish | source
450	```
451	
452	Child process 不能改變 parent working directory，因此受信任的 `shell-init` output 會定義 wrapper。Navigation command 執行時，wrapper 從 private child-only file descriptor 讀取 NUL-terminated path，再呼叫 `builtin cd`；它不會把一般 `dev` command output 當成 shell code evaluate。
